sources.title: Electroencephalography Changes During Cybersickness: Focusing on Delta and Alpha Waves
sources.locator: Introduction, alpha paragraph; EEG Recording and Data Process; Results, alpha paragraph; Discussion, alpha/SSQ paragraphs
sources.excerpt: Occipital alpha (8–13 Hz) decreased during a sickness-inducing video. Alpha direction differs across prior studies; this study found no significant alpha–SSQ association. These observations do not establish a universal severity rule.

sources.title: Cybersickness-induced EEG responses in curved monitor and head-mounted display
sources.locator: EEG recording and data process; Results, Evaluate cybersickness within each display, Tables 1–2; Discussion, alpha/theta/beta/gamma and final EEG–SSQ paragraphs
sources.excerpt: In 31 susceptible young men, alpha decreased during both displays. Theta and beta changes depended on region and display. Frontal gamma used 30–50 Hz. No EEG–SSQ measure was significantly correlated. Sensory-conflict interpretation remains an explanatory hypothesis.
sources.review_note: Publication year is 2026 although the DOI contains 025. Tables and narrative disagree for central gamma in curved-VR; no central-gamma direction is admitted. Both Lee papers share one independence group.

sources.title: Cybersickness-induced EEG responses in curved monitor and head-mounted display
sources.locator: Introduction, sensory conflict paragraph; Discussion, delta sensory-conflict paragraph, beta vestibular paragraph, final EEG–SSQ interpretation paragraph
sources.excerpt: The authors describe visual–vestibular conflict as a widely used theory and propose that EEG responses reflect visual processing load during conflict resolution. The beta/vestibular interpretation is tentative; EEG is not a direct vestibular or cognitive-load measurement.

sources.title: Toward Accurate Cybersickness Prediction in Virtual Reality: A Multimodal Physiological Modeling Approach
sources.locator: Abstract; Section 2.1.3 Apparatus and Data Collection; Section 4.2 Feature Importance and Physiological Mechanism Analysis; Section 4.4 Limitations and Future Directions
sources.excerpt: EDA and ECG features were studied in VR navigation. Skin-conductance features were associated with predicted VRSQ severity and interpreted as sympathetic arousal. This supports autonomic context, but not an EEG-only autonomic inference or external generalization of reported performance.

sources.title: Multimodal Contrastive Learning for Cybersickness Recognition Using Brain Connectivity Graph Representation
sources.excerpt: The abstract introduces EEG, video, and motion connectivity representations for recognition. It does not establish a specific observed EEG connectivity direction or a biomarker-to-mechanism relationship for this project.
verification_methods: Europe PMC PubMed indexed metadata and abstract
sources.review_note: Full text and target feature definition not verified; excluded from reviewed graph.

sources.title: Project raw EEG observation and frozen path-model protocol
sources.locator: eeg_agent/tools.py:BANDS, _spectral, _covariance; eeg_agent/online/features.py:BANDS; vrms knowledge cards, raw-only protocol and spectral/CSP sections
sources.excerpt: Measured bands are theta 4–8 Hz, alpha 8–13 Hz, beta 13–30 Hz, gamma_low 30–45 Hz. Online path model uses four bands through beta. Tool scores are learned outputs rather than physiological biomarker directions; covariance is not directed functional connectivity. No resting baseline is assumed for raw path classification.

sources.title: Candidate inventory and unsupported transfer boundaries
sources.locator: README.md, candidate inventory and review boundaries
sources.excerpt: EEG entropy has no verified disease-specific relation in this MVP. Connectivity lacks verified compatible observations and mechanistic direction. Published 30–50 Hz gamma is not interchangeable with gamma_low 30–45 Hz. Candidate concepts are inventory items and cannot enter retrieval.
verification_methods: No compatible reviewed claim found in this limited search
sources.review_note: A search gap is not evidence that a biomarker lacks an association.
